reviews.review:
Stellar. A total knockout.

Here's what this game is NOT: it's not a next-gen, new school Metroidvania in the mold of Hollow Knight, 9 Souls or Blasphemous. Nowadays, modern entries into the genre prioritize vast, labyrinthine, exploration-driven experiences combined with souls-like combat... and while they're cool (and sometimes downright incredible), they play nothing like the side-scrolling platformers I grew up on in the 80s and 90s. Many modern Metroidvanias feature retro aesthetics, but there's little/nothing about them which play like arcade classics or the NES, SNES and Genesis games I grew up on.

That's fine, but I realized a while ago that while games like Hollow Knight are gorgeous achievements, they don't scratch my itches. I'm a busy guy with a career and a family - I don't have the bandwidth to chart my way across massive, borderline open-world platform mazes. I can't spend all night backtracking with various keys and learning the lightning-fast attack patterns of dozens of mini-bosses. I need simpler pleasures.

Shinobi 2 is a perfectly-calibrated masterpiece of arcade-style platforming action, straight up. There's exploration, sure, and there are areas to unlock and spaces to revisit, but the game ultimately propels the player through a linear series of levels that play with all the vintage tropes: a moving train; a vast underground lab; a mountain ascent. Enemies are occasionally difficult, but there's nothing souls-like about any of this - instead, the developers prioritized combat that feels explosive, satisfying and fun, just challenging enough to demand your focus but never punishing.

In every respect, it feels like a sexy, juiced-up SEGA Genesis title - expansive and updated enough to be worth your time as a modern gamer, but always geared towards a propulsive, arcade-like adventure that's easy to enjoy and never feels like a job.

For the right kind of gamer looking for a nostalgic blast, it's a pure 10/10.
